subject: Food Science
title: Oxygen and Oxidation
description: A quick win: understand Oxygen and Oxidation.

hook.text: A bag of chips is mostly nitrogen gas—not air. Oxygen would turn the oils rancid within weeks.

buildup.text: Oxidation breaks down unsaturated fats into aldehydes and ketones—volatile compounds with stale, cardboard-like off-flavors.

discovery.text: Modified atmosphere packaging (MAP) replaces air with nitrogen or CO₂. Meat stays red, lettuce stays crisp.

twist.text: Vacuum packaging removes air but can create an anaerobic environment perfect for botulism in certain foods.

climax.text: Antioxidants like vitamin E and rosemary extract are added to oils and meat to block oxidation chemically.

punchline.text: Remove the oxygen or block its chemistry. Either way, freshness stays.

quiz.question: Why are chip bags filled with nitrogen instead of air?
options: Nitrogen prevents oxygen from turning oils rancid
